For a while she sat in her arm-chair, opening and shutting the absurd ivory fan between her mittened fingers; but suddenly she lifted her head and listened.

Of now a spotted Hydra-skin cast off,
And now a screen of carven ivory
That shuts the heavens’ conventual secrets up

To the tune o’ those Weary Blues.
With his ebony hands on each ivory key
He made that poor piano moan with melody.
I remember a girl,--how pretty she was, with the crimson flooding the old ivory of her cheeks and her gracious plumpness!

The box of presents she had brought for her California friends had been opened the evening before; and silks, embroideries, carved ivories, ornamental lacquer-ware, brasses, camphorwood boxes, fans, and chinaware were scattered around in confused heaps.
ivors: “And haven’t you your own land to visit,” continued Miss Ivors, “that you know nothing of, your own people, and your own country?”
It shot through Gabriel’s mind that Miss Ivors was not there and that she had gone away discourteously: and he said with confidence in himself:
“But you will come, won’t you?” said Miss Ivors, laying her warm hand eagerly on his arm.
On the landing outside the drawing-room Gabriel found his wife and Mary Jane trying to persuade Miss Ivors to stay for supper.
“Ever so much, I assure you,” said Miss Ivors, “but you really must let me run off now.”
“And haven’t you your own language to keep in touch with—Irish?” asked Miss Ivors.
